sana: Observed an odd reconnect pattern on prod streaming: clients start SSE, then after an idle proxy 60s timeout they unexpectedly upgrade to WS fallback and we end up creating a second session (duplicate billing + missing resume visibility). Anyone seen this? :eyes:
liam: saw similar traces earlier. proxy returns 408-ish then client reconnects. server treats WS as a new session when X-Resume-Id is missing.
noah: can you paste a sample header dump + proxy log? suspect proxy is normalizing/removing resume header on upgrade.
sana: paste log snippet:
```
[edge-proxy] 2026-03-18T12:01:02Z client=10.1.2.3 method=GET path=/v1/stream status=408 idle=61 upgrade=websocket
headers: {Host: api.redwood.ai, Connection: keep-alive, Upgrade: websocket, X-Resume-Id: "rsm_abc123"}
[edge-proxy] 2026-03-18T12:01:03Z client=10.1.2.3 method=GET path=/v1/stream status=101 upgrade=websocket
headers: {Host: api.redwood.ai, Connection: Upgrade, Upgrade: websocket}
```
liam: that second request has X-Resume-Id missing. our WS-handshake code path currently looks only at X-Resume-Id header and not at the opaque session cookie mapping. if header stripped -> new session created. :thinking_face:
maria: business question: is this responsible for the ~12% token usage bump we saw in the last 30m?
sana: yes, correlates to tenant xzy-corp and route /v1/stream. console shows two concurrent session ids for same user but streaming dashboard only shows the second one.
noah: root cause hypothesis: certain proxy variants drop custom headers on upgrade. mitigation options:
  - A) teach edge proxy to preserve X-Resume-Id/header during upgrade (ops/config)
  - B) make WS resume logic fallback to KVCACHE lookup using opaque cookie/session id (app-level resilient fix)
I prefer B since it protects against any intermediate proxy.
sara-oncall: paging oncall, tagging incident runbook -> https://redwood.docs/runbooks/sse-reconnect. Paging so we can rollback if rollout causes regressions. :rotating_light:
incidents-bot: Incident created INC-2026-042 by sara-oncall at 2026-03-18T12:05:00Z
liam: quick patch idea: in router middleware, when handling WS handshake do:
```
if (!resumeId && cookie.session_id) {
  resumeId = kvcache.lookup(cookie.session_id)
}
```
small change, low risk, canary quickly.
sana: canary on canary-2 (us-east-1) please. will monitor duplicate-session-rate and token counts.
deploy-bot: deploy started to canary-2 by liam (deploy id 1234)
liam: pushed canary, adding telemetry tag 'resume_source' = 'cookie-fallback' when we fill resumeId from cookie so console can surface missing header cases.
noah: also adding counters: resume_header_missing, resume_cookie_fallback, duplicate_session_detected. will wire to console dashboard.
maria: please add an aggregate panel for resume_source and a duplicate-session-rate metric; set alert if duplicate-session-rate for any tenant > 1%. business needs to know quickly.
liam: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/789 (small change + unit tests)
sana: after canary at 20% traffic duplicate-session-rate dropped from 4.7% -> 0.2% for affected tenant. token usage trend normalized. :tada:
sara-oncall: holding until full rollout completes; thanks for the fast turnaround. :+1:
noah: long-term note: unify session acquisition in router middleware so all ingress paths (SSE, WS, HTTP reconnects) consult same kvcache/resume lookup and record resume_source telemetry. also add e2e with an nginx variant that strips headers to avoid regressions.
liam: created infra ticket infra-1423 to add nginx header-stripping test and a console alert dashboard work item.
maria: great. once full rollout verifies, can we add a short blameless postmortem doc summarizing action items and owner? i'll open postmortem-INC-2026-042.
sana: ack, will write short summary and link to PR + dashboard.
liam: on it. closing loop once deploy reaches 100% and alerts remain green.
